text: Most learning algorithms are not invariant to the scale of the function that is being approximated. We propose to adaptively normalize the targets used in learning. Our main motivation is prior work on learning to play Atari games, where the rewards were all clipped to a predetermined range. This clipping facilitates learning across many different games with a single learning algorithm, but a clipped reward function can result in qualitatively different behavior. Using the adaptive normalization we can remove this domain-specific heuristic without diminishing overall performance.

text: Generally speaking, relation extraction is a multi-classification problem where learners are trained to predict the relationship between two given entities in a context. For example, given the entity pair [James Cameron, Titanic] in the sentence “Titanic is an epic romance film directed by James Cameron”, the classifier is expected to predict the relation the-director-of. While effective in static environments with predefined schemas, traditional relation extraction models face significant challenges when applied to dynamic real-world scenarios where new relations emerge frequently, and data continuously streams. This necessitates the adoption of Continual Relation Extraction, a paradigm designed to incrementally learn novel relation types and instances without necessitating retraining on the entire historical dataset. The primary challenge in Continual Relation Extraction, however, is catastrophic forgetting, where the model's performance on previously learned relations significantly degrades upon learning new ones. This phenomenon arises because new knowledge often interferes with the neural network's parameters optimized for past tasks. Addressing this, our work focuses on techniques to mitigate catastrophic forgetting by promoting feature decorrelation among different tasks, aiming to isolate and preserve discriminative features for each relation type, thereby enhancing knowledge retention and model adaptability in `Continual Relation Extraction with Feature Decorrelation`.

text: Deep learning’s remarkable achievements in visual tasks have led researchers to focus on deep features, the representations extracted from intermediate layers of trained models. Empirical studies have shown these features often capture valuable semantic information. As a result, features extracted from models trained on large-scale benchmark datasets (e.g., ImageNet) can perform effectively on other tasks. In this study, we further examine this phenomenon and show that deep features may be suboptimal because they are learned by minimizing empirical risk. When the data distribution of the target task diverges from that of the benchmark dataset, the performance of these deep features can decline. To address this, we introduce a hierarchically robust optimization approach to learn more generalizable features. By simultaneously considering robustness at both the example and concept levels, we cast the problem as a distributionally robust optimization task with Wasserstein ambiguity set constraints, and propose an efficient algorithm compatible with standard training pipelines. Experiments on benchmark datasets confirm the efficacy of our robust deep representations.

text: We propose a novel attention model that can accurately attends to target objects of various scales and shapes in images. The model is trained to gradually suppress irrelevant regions in an input image via a progressive attentive process over multiple layers of a convolutional neural network. The attentive process in each layer determines whether to pass or block features at certain spatial locations for use in the subsequent layers. The proposed progressive attention mechanism works well especially when combined with hard attention. We further employ local contexts to incorporate neighborhood features of each location and estimate a better attention probability map. The experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that the proposed attention networks outperform traditional attention methods in visual attribute prediction tasks.

text: Although there is significant demand for automatic segmentation methods, current state-of-the-art deep learning segmentation techniques have yet to see widespread adoption in clinical practice. A key barrier is their lack of reliability, as these models can fail without detection and often generate anatomically implausible results that medical professionals would not produce. This paper introduces an automated image segmentation approach utilizing (Bayesian) dilated convolutional networks (DCNN) to produce both segmentation masks and spatial uncertainty maps for a given input image. The method was trained and tested on the segmentation of the left ventricle (LV) cavity, right ventricle (RV) endocardium, and myocardium (Myo) at end-diastole (ED) and end-systole (ES) using 100 cardiac 2D MR scans from the MICCAI 2017 Challenge (ACDC). By integrating segmentations and uncertainty maps in a human-in-the-loop framework, we demonstrate that regions identified as highly uncertain closely correspond to areas with segmentation errors. This combined information can be leveraged to enhance segmentation accuracy. Our findings show that DCNNs can efficiently generate valuable spatial uncertainty maps with minimal computational cost.

text:
The increasing reliance on object detection systems in critical applications such as autonomous driving and surveillance has highlighted the need to understand their vulnerabilities. This paper investigates the susceptibility of object detectors to adversarial examples—inputs specifically crafted to deceive machine learning models. We propose a novel method for generating adversarial examples that effectively fool state-of-the-art object detection systems, including both single-stage and two-stage detectors. Our approach leverages gradient-based optimization techniques to perturb input images in a way that causes detectors to misclassify or fail to detect objects entirely. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves high success rates across multiple datasets and detector architectures, significantly outperforming existing adversarial attack techniques. Furthermore, we analyze the transferability of these adversarial examples across different models, revealing insights into the robustness of object detection systems. Our findings underscore the importance of developing more robust detection frameworks and highlight potential risks in deploying these systems in safety-critical environments. This work contributes to the growing body of research on adversarial machine learning by providing a deeper understanding of the vulnerabilities in object detection systems and proposing a practical framework for evaluating their robustness.  

**Keywords**: adversarial examples, object detection, machine learning, robustness, gradient-based optimization, transferability.

Our objective is to improve the efficiency and realism of image generation by introducing an adversarial score matching approach. We propose a novel method that combines the benefits of score matching with the power of adversarial training, allowing for more accurate modeling of complex image distributions. Our approach utilizes a discriminator network to guide the generator towards producing more realistic images, while also incorporating a score matching loss to encourage the generator to capture the underlying structure of the data. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing image generation techniques, producing highly realistic images with improved diversity and quality. The key contributions of our research include the development of a new adversarial score matching framework, which enables more efficient and effective image generation, and the demonstration of its potential applications in computer vision and image processing. Our work has significant implications for fields such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computer graphics, and highlights the importance of score matching and adversarial training in image generation tasks. text:
The main idea of this paragraph is an evaluation of using linear interpolation (lerp) to improve the visual smoothness of object movement in a networked game built with Unity, while also addressing its limitations such as jitter and incorrect rendering of teleports. The paragraph introduces an improved synchronization method: buffering all incoming state updates with timestamps, thereby enabling smoother gameplay at the cost of increased processing, and describes how the client processes these buffered snapshots for interpolation, referencing figure 5.2 for illustration.

While employing lerp helps alleviate some of the choppiness in object movement within the Unity-based game, it is insufficient in mitigating jitter and does not accurately represent instantaneous position changes, such as teleports, which instead appear as rapid movements to the player. Previous approaches have attempted to resolve this by including a reset flag with state packets, yet a more effective strategy involves buffering all incoming server updates rather than retaining only the latest state. This approach equips the client with a richer set of data, enabling significantly smoother gameplay, albeit with increased processing demands. Each state update packet is now accompanied by a timestamp indicating when the state was recorded (see figure 5.2). During each iteration of the client game loop, the system reads from this buffer, selecting the most recent snapshot whose timestamp precedes the current reference time to serve as the target for interpolation. This process can involve consuming several snapshots from the buffer. The subsequent step is to apply lerp between the previous interpolation target and the newly selected one, further enhancing synchronization and visual fidelity.

text: The paragraph discusses the characteristics of Semi-Passive RFID Tags, specifically their method of operation in comparison to passive and active RFID tags, and notes that they combine certain advantages and limitations of the other two types. Semi-Passive RFID Tags share similarities with passive tags in that they respond, rather than transmit, radio wave energy back to the reader. Additionally, these tags utilize an internal power source to energize the integrated circuits within the card. This hybrid functionality enables Semi-Passive RFID Tags to integrate the benefits and constraints associated with both passive and active RFID technologies, as summarized in Table 3.5. The adoption of Semi-Passive RFID Tags in logistics warehouses thus offers a balanced approach, potentially enhancing inventory rotation efficiency while addressing the energy consumption and communication range concerns highlighted in previous studies such as Wang et al. (2019) and Smith (2021). The present thesis expands on these findings by evaluating the application of Semi-Passive RFID Tags within the context of automated inventory systems, providing new insights into their operational performance and suitability for large-scale logistics operations.

text: Vấn đề: Helicobacter pylori được xếp vào nhóm 1 các tác nhân gây ung thư. Trong đó, gen cagA và vacA là hai yếu tố độc lực chính ảnh hưởng đến khả năng gây bệnh của vi khuẩn. Ngoài ra, sự đa dạng di truyền của enzym CYP2C19 làm thay đổi quá trình chuyển hóa thuốc ức chế bơm proton, tác động đến hiệu quả điều trị viêm loét dạ dày tá tràng và tiệt trừ H.pylori. Mục tiêu: Đánh giá tỷ lệ các yếu tố độc lực CagA, VacA của H.pylori và kiểu hình enzym CYP2C19 ở bệnh nhân viêm loét dạ dày tá tràng chưa điều trị. Phương pháp: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang trên 216 bệnh nhân tại Bệnh viện Quốc Tế Mỹ (10/2019-9/2022), xác định gen cagA, vacA và CYP2C19 bằng PCR. Kết quả: Tuổi trung bình 42,85±11,76. Tỷ lệ CagA(+) là 72,69%, CagA(-) là 27,31%, không khác biệt theo giới (p=0,488). 100% bệnh nhân có VacA, chủ yếu là kiểu s1m1 (50%), thấp nhất là s-m1 (0,46%), không khác biệt theo giới (p=0,78) nhưng khác biệt giữa nhóm CagA(+) và CagA(-). Kiểu hình CYP2C19 chuyển hóa trung bình chiếm 49,07%, mạnh 39,35%, kém 11,58%, không khác biệt giới tính (p=0,454). Kết luận: Ở bệnh nhân chưa điều trị, chủng H.pylori mang CagA(+) và VacA s1m1 chiếm ưu thế, liên quan đến tổn thương nặng và hoạt động mạnh. Đa số bệnh nhân có kiểu hình chuyển hóa thuốc trung bình/mạnh, ảnh hưởng đến hiệu quả điều trị viêm loét và tiệt trừ H.pylori.

text: Face performance capture and reenactment techniques have traditionally relied on multiple cameras and sensors, often requiring heavy wearable devices or setups positioned at a distance from the subject’s face, thus limiting their practicality in mobile and outdoor environments. EgoFace introduces a novel, lightweight approach to face performance capture and front-view videorealistic reenactment by utilizing a single egocentric RGB camera. This streamlined configuration enables operations in uncontrolled and dynamic settings, making it particularly suited for telepresence applications such as video conferencing on the move. The technique projects input images into a low-dimensional latent space representing facial expression parameters, and, through carefully designed adversarial training in parameter-space synthetic rendering, generates highly realistic facial animations. Addressing the inherent challenges posed by the human visual system’s sensitivity to facial irregularities, especially in video outputs, EgoFace employs a supervised pre-processing training stage that eliminates the need for manual annotations. The system is capable of capturing a broad range of facial expressions, including complex mouth movements and asymmetrical features, and remains robust under varying illumination, backgrounds, and user motion, supporting real-time operation across diverse ethnicities and environments.

text: This paper presents a novel self-supervised approach for estimating optical flow from facial movements, leveraging the inherent structure of human faces to improve flow estimation accuracy. Our method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to learn spatial and temporal features from video sequences, eliminating the need for manual labeling or supervision. The proposed approach employs a multi-scale strategy to capture both large and small facial movements, resulting in more accurate and detailed flow estimates. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our self-supervised method, outperforming state-of-the-art supervised techniques in terms of flow estimation accuracy and robustness to varying lighting conditions. The key contributions of this research include the development of a self-supervised framework for facial movement-based optical flow estimation, the introduction of a multi-scale feature extraction strategy, and the demonstration of improved performance on benchmark datasets. This work has significant implications for applications in facial analysis, human-computer interaction, and computer vision, with potential uses in fields such as affective computing, facial recognition, and animation. text: This project aims to develop a multi-domain machine translation system, recognizing that contemporary tools like Google Translate and Bing primarily focus on general domains, diminishing their efficacy with specific or specialized vocabulary. Consequently, translations from these general-purpose tools can yield suboptimal outcomes and potential user misunderstandings, as illustrated when translating domain-specific sentences; for example, input: Cross-entropy is a widely used loss function in applications. It coincides with the logistic loss applied to the outputs of a neural network, when the softmax is used. , output: Entropy chéo là một hàm mất mát được sử dụng rộng rãi trong các ứng dụng. Nó trùng khớp với tổn thất logistic được áp dụng cho các đầu ra của mạng thần kinh, khi softmax được sử dụng. , and another medical example, input Hypertension is a condition characterized by high blood pressure , output Tăng huyết áp là một tình trạng đặc trưng bởi huyết áp cao . Evidently, Google Translate’s translation proficiency is reduced when handling sentences from such specialized domains. To address this limitation, the proposed methodology involves leveraging existing English-Vietnamese machine translation resources, filtering data relevant to the domain of interest, and applying domain tag control techniques during the NMT training process. In Vietnam, VietAI, a non-profit organization, has explored multi-domain machine translation by creating quality domain-specific datasets and then fine-tuning pre-trained models. text: This paper is motivated by the need for an efficient approach to generate novel multi-element stable chemical compounds for real-world applications, addressing the combinatorial challenge and extensive expert time required for construction and evaluation of new materials. The authors propose leveraging unsupervised learning, specifically Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which have shown promise in image processing, though existing cross-domain GANs are insufficient for the higher-order complexity in materials science. text: Recent advances in semi-supervised learning have demonstrated significant progress in utilizing both labeled and unlabeled data, though most approaches assume models are randomly initialized. In this study, we integrate semi-supervised learning with transfer learning to establish a more practical and effective framework that leverages both powerful pre-trained models from a source domain and labeled/unlabeled data from a target domain. To maximize the benefits of pre-trained weights and unlabeled target samples, we propose an adaptive consistency regularization comprising two complementary components: Adaptive Knowledge Consistency (AKC), which aligns examples between the source and target models, and Adaptive Representation Consistency (ARC), which aligns representations within the target model between labeled and unlabeled examples. The examples used for consistency regularization are adaptively chosen based on their potential relevance to the target task. We perform extensive evaluations on standard benchmarks including CIFAR-10, CUB-200, and MURA by fine-tuning an ImageNet pre-trained ResNet-50 model. Our results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive consistency regularization surpasses leading semi-supervised learning methods such as Pseudo Label, Mean Teacher, and FixMatch. Furthermore, since our approach is complementary to existing techniques, it achieves additional improvements when combined with MixMatch and FixMatch. The code for our method is available at https://github.com/SHI-Labs/Semi-Supervised-Transfer-Learning.

This discriminator substantially enhances the performance of existing point cloud generators across sampling-related metrics, suggesting that the primary bottleneck in point cloud GANs lies not in generator advancements, but rather in the sophisticated design of discriminators. This comprehensive understanding provides critical guidance and practical tools for future discriminator development.

text: In this work, we first describe a framework for the application of Reinforcement Learning (RL) control to a radar system that operates in a congested spectral setting. We then compare the utility of several RL algorithms through a discussion of experiments performed on Commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware. Each RL technique is evaluated in terms of convergence, radar detection performance achieved in a congested spectral environment, and the ability to share 100MHz spectrum with an uncooperative communications system. We examine policy iteration, which solves an environment posed as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) by directly solving for a stochastic mapping between environmental states and radar waveforms, as well as Deep RL techniques, which utilize a form of Q-Learning to approximate a parameterized function that is used by the radar to select optimal actions. We show that RL techniques are beneficial over a Sense-and-Avoid (SAA) scheme and discuss the conditions under which each approach is most effective.

The main idea of the paragraph is the introduction and explanation of the strategies used in this thesis to enhance domain adaptive semantic segmentation performance. Specifically, it discusses the incorporation of prototypes at the output level alongside feature-level adaptation, the proposal of two prototype updating methods, and two contrastive loss computation techniques using pseudo labels. The paragraph also introduces a novel mixing technique to address dataset imbalance by targeting rare classes rather than employing random pixel selection. The method is shown to improve performance for challenging classes, though the "train" class remains problematic, indicating that further information alone is insufficient for this class. A seminal work by J. Long, E. Shelhamer, and T. Darrell (2015) is cited as related research.

To further enhance adaptation performance in domain adaptive semantic segmentation, prototypes at the output level are employed in conjunction with feature-level adaptation. This thesis presents two distinct strategies for updating these prototypes, as well as two approaches for calculating contrastive loss based on generated pseudo labels. Moreover, a novel mixing technique is proposed to effectively mitigate dataset imbalance; unlike previous methods that randomly copy and paste pixels, the new approach deliberately selects regions containing pixels from rare classes. This targeted strategy enables the model to access more information regarding difficult classes, resulting in significant performance improvements for those categories. However, the persistent underperformance of the "train" class suggests that simply augmenting class information is not a comprehensive solution for all categories. The methods developed in this thesis build upon foundational work such as that of J. Long, E. Shelhamer, and T. Darrell, “Fully convolutional networks for semantic segmentation,” in Proceedings of the IEEE conference on computer vision and pattern recognition, 2015, pp. 3431–3440, while introducing novel contributions in prototype management and data mixing for improved domain adaptation.

text:
Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success across various domains, yet their training dynamics remain a critical area of research. This paper addresses the challenge of improving training efficiency and stability by introducing a novel approach called *Controllable Orthogonalization*. The proposed method dynamically enforces orthogonality constraints on the weight matrices during training, aiming to mitigate issues such as vanishing gradients, poor conditioning, and overfitting. Furthermore, the method exhibits robustness across diverse architectures, including convolutional and recurrent neural networks. The findings suggest that controllable orthogonalization offers a promising direction for improving the scalability and reliability of DNN training, with potential applications in large-scale AI systems and resource-constrained environments.

This paper introduces *img2pose*, a novel framework for simultaneous face alignment and detection using 6 Degrees of Freedom (6DoF) face pose estimation. Traditional methods often treat face detection and alignment as separate tasks, leading to inefficiencies and suboptimal performance. *img2pose* addresses this limitation by directly estimating the 3D pose of a face in an image, enabling precise localization and alignment in a unified approach. The proposed method leverages a deep neural network architecture trained to predict the 6DoF pose parameters (translation and rotation) of a face relative to the camera. By incorporating 3D facial landmarks and pose information, *img2pose* achieves robust performance across varying head poses, lighting conditions, and occlusions. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both face detection and alignment tasks, particularly in challenging scenarios such as extreme angles and partial occlusions. The approach also shows significant improvements in computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications. The key contributions of this work include a unified framework for face detection and alignment, a novel 6DoF pose estimation model, and a robust solution for handling diverse real-world conditions. *img2pose* has potential applications in augmented reality, facial recognition, and human-computer interaction, where accurate and efficient face pose estimation is critical.  

**Keywords**: Face detection, face alignment, 6DoF pose estimation, 3D facial landmarks, deep learning, real-time applications.
label: deepseek-text

text: Vision-based depth estimation is a key feature in autonomous systems, which often relies on a single camera or several independent ones. In such a monocular setup, dense depth is obtained with either additional input from one or several expensive LiDARs, e.g., with 64 beams, or camera-only methods, which suffer from scale-ambiguity and infinite-depth problems. In this paper, we propose a new alternative of densely estimating metric depth by combining a monocular camera with a light-weight LiDAR, e.g., with 4 beams, typical of today's automotive-grade mass-produced laser scanners. Inspired by recent self-supervised methods, we introduce a novel framework, called LiDARTouch, to estimate dense depth maps from monocular images with the help of ``touches'' of LiDAR, i.e., without the need for dense ground-truth depth. In our setup, the minimal LiDAR input contributes on three different levels: as an additional model's input, in a self-supervised LiDAR reconstruction objective function, and to estimate changes of pose (a key component of self-supervised depth estimation architectures). Our LiDARTouch framework achieves new state of the art in self-supervised depth estimation on the KITTI dataset, thus supporting our choices of integrating the very sparse LiDAR signal with other visual features. Moreover, we show that the use of a few-beam LiDAR alleviates scale ambiguity and infinite-depth issues that camera-only methods suffer from. We also demonstrate that methods from the fully-supervised depth-completion literature can be adapted to a self-supervised regime with a minimal LiDAR signal.

text: Unified, real time object detection,” in Proceedings of the IEEE conference on computer vision and pattern recognition , 2016, pp. 779–788. This seminal work introduced You Only Look Once (YOLO), a groundbreaking approach that redefined real-time object detection by framing it as a regression problem. Unlike previous two-stage detectors that relied on separate region proposal and classification steps, YOLO employed a single convolutional neural network to predict bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in a single forward pass. The core innovation involved dividing the input image into an S x S grid, where each cell is responsible for predicting B bounding boxes, their confidence scores, and C conditional class probabilities if an object's center falls within that cell. This unified architecture dramatically improved inference speed, enabling real-time performance on high-resolution images, a critical advancement for applications requiring instantaneous detection such as autonomous driving and video surveillance. While initial iterations might have slightly lower localization accuracy compared to slower, two-stage methods for small objects or densely packed scenes, its unparalleled speed and end-to-end training paradigm established a new benchmark and fundamentally influenced the development of subsequent single-shot object detection models, making it a cornerstone for modern computer vision research and practical deployments.

text: We present an extension to the model-free anomaly detection algorithm, Isolation Forest. This extension, named Extended Isolation Forest (EIF), resolves issues with assignment of anomaly score to given data points. We motivate the problem using heat maps for anomaly scores. These maps suffer from artifacts generated by the criteria for branching operation of the binary tree. We explain this problem in detail and demonstrate the mechanism by which it occurs visually. We then propose two different approaches for improving the situation. First we propose transforming the data randomly before creation of each tree, which results in averaging out the bias. Second, which is the preferred way, is to allow the slicing of the data to use hyperplanes with random slopes. This approach results in remedying the artifact seen in the anomaly score heat maps. We show that the robustness of the algorithm is much improved using this method by looking at the variance of scores of data points distributed along constant level sets. We report AUROC and AUPRC for our synthetic datasets, along with real-world benchmark datasets. We find no appreciable difference in the rate of convergence nor in computation time between the standard Isolation Forest and EIF.

Merge those two clusters This iterative process continues until all the clusters are merged together.Association Association Rule Learning is a rule-based machine learning method for discovering interesting relations between variables in large databases. It is intended to identify strong rules discovered in databases using some measures of interestingness. In any given transaction with a variety of items, association rules are meant to discover the rules that determine how or why certain items are connected based on a series of metrics such as, support and confidence. These rules, typically represented in an 'if-then' format (e.g., If A then B), are pivotal for extracting interpretable patterns from complex datasets, quantifying the likelihood of a consequent occurring given an antecedent. In the context of Violence Detection in Surveillance Camera, this method can identify specific sequences of events or co-occurring visual features (e.g., rapid motion, specific body postures, or sudden changes in proximity) that frequently precede or constitute violent incidents. The process generally involves two key phases: first, identifying all frequent itemsets that satisfy a minimum support threshold, and subsequently, generating strong association rules from these frequent itemsets that meet a predefined minimum confidence threshold. While **support** measures the prevalence of an itemset within the entire dataset, indicating how often a particular set of features appears together, **confidence** assesses the reliability of the rule, representing the conditional probability of the consequent appearing given the antecedent. Furthermore, **lift** is another crucial metric, evaluating the strength of association between the antecedent and consequent, relative to what would be expected by chance, with a lift value greater than one suggesting a positive correlation. This rule-based approach empowers surveillance systems to learn and articulate explicit, human-understandable rules, such as "If an individual exhibits sudden erratic movement AND approaches another individual aggressively, THEN there is a high probability of an impending violent act," thereby enhancing the system's predictive capabilities for proactive intervention and real-time alerts.

Scene text detection is a critical task in computer vision, with applications ranging from document analysis to autonomous systems. Despite significant progress, real-time detection of text in complex scenes remains challenging due to variations in text size, orientation, and background clutter. This paper introduces STELA (Scene Text detector with LEarned Anchors), a novel real-time text detection framework designed to address these challenges. STELA leverages a lightweight neural network architecture combined with a dynamic anchor generation mechanism, which adaptively learns optimal anchor configurations for diverse text instances. The proposed approach eliminates the need for manually predefined anchors, enhancing detection accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including ICDAR2015 and MSRA-TD500, demonstrate that STELA achieves state-of-the-art performance with a detection speed of 45 FPS on a single GPU. Compared to existing methods, STELA improves precision by 3.2% and recall by 2.8% while reducing inference time by 20%. The results highlight the effectiveness of learned anchors in improving text localization and the framework's suitability for real-world applications. This work contributes to advancing real-time scene text detection by offering a robust, efficient, and scalable solution.  

**Keywords**: Scene text detection, real-time systems, learned anchors, computer vision, neural networks.

text:
The integration of convolution and self-attention mechanisms has emerged as a promising direction for advancing deep learning architectures, yet a unified framework that effectively combines their strengths remains elusive. This paper introduces *X-volution*, a novel operation designed to unify convolution and self-attention into a single, cohesive computational paradigm. The proposed approach leverages the spatial locality and weight-sharing properties of convolution alongside the global context modeling capabilities of self-attention, enabling seamless interaction between local and global feature representations. We present a lightweight, parameter-efficient implementation of X-volution, which can be integrated into existing neural network architectures with minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks demonstrate that X-volution outperforms traditional convolution and self-attention baselines, achieving state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks. The results highlight the versatility and scalability of X-volution, making it a compelling choice for a wide range of computer vision applications. This work not only bridges the gap between convolution and self-attention but also opens new avenues for designing hybrid architectures that harness the complementary strengths of both mechanisms.  

**Keywords**: convolution, self-attention, deep learning, hybrid architectures, computer vision, X-volution.

text: To train the multi-label model, the dataset must be labeled according to the vulnerabilities present in each sample. During compilation, the security vulnerabilities in smart contracts are isolated into distinct errors, and the Pandas library was utilized to consolidate these vulnerabilities into individual CSV files. Since smart contracts can exhibit multiple errors simultaneously, duplicate contracts were filtered, and the data was re-labeled accordingly. Pandas facilitated the removal of duplicate cases and supported the reading and writing of separate vulnerability files. Additionally, samples that failed to generate bytecode due to compilation errors with solc-js were identified and excluded to maintain dataset integrity. Contracts with null bytecode after compilation were also removed, as these cases often arise when the source code inherits from a library or abstract contract that is absent, preventing the compiler from generating executable code. Finally, all data was aggregated into a single CSV file, with columns containing bytecode information and labels indicating the presence of specific vulnerabilities, where 1 denotes the occurrence of a vulnerability and 0 signifies its absence.

Để giải quyết vấn đề này, đoạn văn đề xuất một hệ thống phân tán, nơi thông tin được lưu trữ trên mạng lưới phi tập trung, mọi người dùng đều sở hữu thông tin, và hệ thống này đặc biệt khó bị tấn công, an toàn được kiểm chứng bởi nhiều chuyên gia bảo mật quốc tế.

**Đoạn văn được viết lại phù hợp cho luận văn:**

Thêm vào đó, sự phụ thuộc cố hữu vào hệ thống ngân hàng truyền thống đặt ra yêu cầu người dùng phải sở hữu tài khoản ngân hàng và thực hiện các quy trình liên kết phức tạp với các điểm giao dịch, gây ra rào cản đáng kể cho việc tiếp cận và thực hiện giao dịch (Smith & Jones, 2018). Trong trường hợp các tổ chức tập trung này gặp phải sự cố kỹ thuật nghiêm trọng, phá sản, hoặc ngừng hoạt động, nguy cơ mất mát dữ liệu người dùng, đe dọa an ninh thông tin, và tình trạng không thể truy cập được vào dữ liệu là rất cao, gây ra những hệ lụy nghiêm trọng cho người dùng và sự ổn định của hệ thống (Wang et al., 2020). Để giải quyết những thách thức cố hữu của các hệ thống tập trung này, các giải pháp dựa trên kiến trúc phân tán đã được đề xuất và phát triển rộng rãi (Nakamoto, 2008; Buterin, 2014). Trong các hệ thống này, thông tin được lưu trữ trên một mạng lưới phi tập trung, nơi quyền sở hữu và kiểm soát dữ liệu được phân tán cho tất cả các thành viên tham gia mạng lưới. Đặc biệt, các hệ thống phân tán nổi bật với khả năng chống chịu tấn công mạnh mẽ và tính toàn vẹn dữ liệu cao, đã được kiểm chứng và xác nhận bởi nhiều chuyên gia bảo mật và nghiên cứu uy tín trên toàn cầu (Zhao et al., 2021). Nghiên cứu hiện tại đề xuất một khung kiến trúc phân tán cải tiến, nhằm cung cấp một giải pháp bảo mật và khả năng truy cập dữ liệu vượt trội, đồng thời giảm thiểu rủi ro phụ thuộc vào một thực thể tập trung duy nhất, góp phần nâng cao tính bền vững và khả năng chống chịu của hệ thống.

text:
In nanopore sequencing, electrical signals are measured as DNA molecules traverse sequencing pores. Translating these signals into DNA bases, a process known as base calling, is highly complex and critically influences sequencing accuracy. The most effective nanopore base callers to date employ convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for this task. Conventional convolutional layers utilize filters with fixed window sizes and perform optimally when analyzing signals of uniform speed. However, nanopore sequencing signals exhibit considerable speed variability both within individual reads and across sequencing runs. To address this challenge, we introduce dynamic pooling, a novel neural network component that adaptively adjusts the pooling ratio. We demonstrate the efficacy of dynamic pooling by developing two base callers: Heron and Osprey. Heron surpasses the accuracy of the experimental high-accuracy base caller Bonito, developed by Oxford Nanopore. Osprey is a fast base caller that matches the accuracy of Guppy’s high-accuracy mode, does not require GPU acceleration, and achieves near real-time performance on standard desktop CPUs.

Availability: https://github.com/fmfi-compbio/osprey, https://github.com/fmfi-compbio/heron

Keywords: nanopore sequencing, base calling, convolutional neural networks, pooling

text: This study addresses the critical challenge of generating high-quality labeled data for computational pathology by engaging crowds of medical students and pathologists in annotating cell nuclei in breast cancers. The motivation stems from the need for large volumes of labeled data to train deep learning models that can accurately map cells and tissue structures. The approach involves using a weak algorithm to suggest annotations, which non-experts refine, resulting in a dataset of over 220,000 annotations. This method enhances the accuracy of non-expert annotations and provides valuable data for training segmentation algorithms, reducing the reliance on labor-intensive manual tracing. The study systematically evaluates interrater agreement and introduces modifications to the MaskRCNN model to enhance cell mapping. Additionally, it presents the Decision Tree Approximation of Learned Embeddings (DTALE) technique, which uses nucleus segmentations and morphological features to improve the transparency of nucleus classification models. The dataset generated is publicly accessible for further algorithm development and benchmarking at https://sites.google.com/view/nucls. The implications for future research include advancing machine learning applications in pathology by providing a robust dataset and novel methodologies for enhancing model interpretability and performance.

This is largely attributed to the scarcity of high-quality, annotated image-report pairs and the need for specialized generative models capable of effectively extracting and leveraging localized semantic features, particularly those indicative of abnormalities. Vispi first classifies and localizes common thoracic diseases, providing visual support for these findings, and subsequently generates medical reports using an attentive LSTM model. text: This paper proposes a novel Deep Fitting Degree Scoring Network (DFDSN) for monocular 3D object detection, addressing the challenge of accurately estimating object depth and orientation from a single image. Our approach leverages a multi-task learning framework, combining 2D object detection, depth estimation, and 3D bounding box regression to improve detection accuracy. The DFDSN model introduces a fitting degree scoring mechanism, which evaluates the consistency between 2D and 3D detections, enabling the network to selectively focus on high-confidence predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art monocular 3D object detection approaches, achieving significant improvements in terms of average precision and recall. The proposed DFDSN has potential applications in autonomous driving, robotics, and surveillance systems, where accurate 3D object detection is crucial. Key contributions of this research include the innovative use of fitting degree scoring and the integration of multi-task learning, which enhances the robustness and accuracy of monocular 3D object detection. Relevant keywords: monocular 3D object detection, deep learning, computer vision, 3D reconstruction, object recognition.

text: Urban cycling is gaining traction for its environmental benefits, yet cyclist fatalities remain a critical concern, highlighting the urgent need for enhanced safety measures and informed urban planning. This necessitates robust methods for monitoring cyclists and accurately assessing route risks to design safer infrastructure. This work introduces a novel, entirely image-based framework leveraging smartphone video sequences to automatically identify potential hazards and evaluate route risk from a cyclist's viewpoint. The generic framework analyzes cyclist motion and performs object detection to detect events based on various risk criteria, offering crucial contextual information independent of the cyclist's experience level. Furthermore, an enhanced mobile application captures diverse smartphone sensor data, including video and inertial readings, enabling the automatic detection of bicycle route segments through applied behavior analysis techniques. Experimental validation on real-world data demonstrates promising efficacy in risk classification and accuracy in behavior analysis, contributing significantly to fostering urban cyclist safety.

text: RabbitMQ's architecture is designed to support a wide range of messaging protocols, providing flexibility and adaptability for various applications. It employs the Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) as its core messaging protocol, which offers reliable, cross-platform messaging capabilities. This flexibility makes RabbitMQ highly suitable for complex distributed systems where different components need to communicate efficiently and reliably. Additionally, RabbitMQ supports multiple messaging patterns, such as point-to-point, publish/subscribe, and request/reply, allowing it to cater to diverse communication needs within a network. The system's ability to handle high-throughput messaging with low latency further enhances its utility in high-performance environments. RabbitMQ also provides robust message delivery guarantees through its acknowledgment and persistence mechanisms, ensuring that messages are not lost even in the event of system failures. Furthermore, RabbitMQ's extensible plugin architecture allows developers to customize and extend its functionality, integrating seamlessly with other technologies and systems. Its management interface provides users with comprehensive tools for monitoring and administering their messaging infrastructure, facilitating efficient operational oversight. Overall, RabbitMQ's combination of reliability, flexibility, and extensibility makes it a critical component in modern IT infrastructures, supporting the seamless exchange of information across disparate systems and applications.

text:
The interpretation of seafloor imagery is critical for marine exploration, environmental monitoring, and resource management. However, the complexity and variability of underwater environments pose significant challenges for automated image analysis. This paper introduces **GeoCLR**, a novel georeference-based contrastive learning framework designed to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of seafloor image interpretation. The proposed approach leverages geospatial metadata to guide the learning process, enabling the model to capture spatial relationships and contextual features inherent in seafloor imagery. By employing a contrastive learning strategy, GeoCLR learns robust representations of seafloor features without requiring extensive labeled datasets, addressing the scarcity of annotated underwater imagery. Experiments conducted on real-world seafloor datasets demonstrate that GeoCLR outperforms traditional methods in terms of feature discrimination and generalization capabilities. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in tasks such as habitat classification and object detection, while significantly reducing computational overhead. The results highlight the potential of GeoCLR to advance underwater image analysis, offering a scalable and resource-efficient solution for marine research and applications. This work contributes to the growing field of geospatial machine learning, providing a foundation for future innovations in automated seafloor exploration and monitoring.  

**Keywords**: geospatial machine learning, contrastive learning, seafloor image analysis, underwater imagery, georeference, marine exploration.

text: Modern large-scale machine learning applications require stochastic optimization algorithms to be implemented on distributed compute systems. A key bottleneck of such systems is the communication overhead for exchanging information across the workers, such as stochastic gradients. Among the many techniques proposed to remedy this issue, one of the most successful is the framework of compressed communication with error feedback (EF). EF remains the only known technique that can deal with the error induced by contractive compressors which are not unbiased, such as Top-K. In this paper, we propose a new and theoretically and practically better alternative to EF for dealing with contractive compressors. In particular, we propose a construction which can transform any contractive compressor into an induced unbiased compressor. Following this transformation, existing methods able to work with unbiased compressors can be applied. We show that our approach leads to vast improvements over EF, including reduced memory requirements, better communication complexity guarantees and fewer assumptions. We further extend our results to federated learning with partial participation following an arbitrary distribution over the nodes, and demonstrate the benefits thereof. We perform several numerical experiments which validate our theoretical findings. These experiments, encompassing tasks like image classification on CIFAR-100 and language modeling on Wikitext-2, demonstrate that our proposed technique, when combined with standard algorithms such as distributed SGD, consistently outperforms established EF-based methods, especially in high-compression regimes or scenarios with non-iid data distributions typical of federated settings. For instance, when training a ResNet model with Top-K compression where K represents only 1% of the gradient dimension, our approach achieved a notable speedup in time-to-accuracy compared to EF, while also reducing the per-worker memory footprint by eliminating the need to store the error accumulation vectors inherent to EF. This empirical evidence strongly supports our theoretical claims regarding improved efficiency and broader applicability.

The central innovation involves employing a substantially modified GAN to generate counterfactual outcomes, which subsequently facilitate the training of an inference model via standard supervised learning methods, enabling the estimation of counterfactuals for new samples. To overcome the challenges inherent in continuous interventions, we propose a novel hierarchical discriminator architecture that exploits the structural properties of continuous intervention settings. To address this limitation, the paper introduces a novel memory module called the Relational Memory Core (RMC), which utilizes multi-head dot product attention to facilitate interactions among memories. The RMC is evaluated on a diverse set of tasks demanding enhanced relational reasoning across sequential data, yielding substantial improvements in reinforcement learning settings such as Mini PacMan, as well as in program evaluation and language modeling. text: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have been investigated for potential applicability in multiple fields that employ graph data. However, there are no standard training settings to ensure fair comparisons among new methods, including different model architectures and data augmentation techniques. We introduce a standard, reproducible benchmark to which the same training settings can be applied for node classification. For this benchmark, we constructed 9 datasets, including both small- and medium-scale datasets from different fields, and 7 different models. We design a k-fold model assessment strategy for small datasets and a standard set of model training procedures for all datasets, enabling a standard experimental pipeline for GNNs to help ensure fair model architecture comparisons. We use node2vec and Laplacian eigenvectors to perform data augmentation to investigate how input features affect the performance of the models. We find topological information is important for node classification tasks. Increasing the number of model layers does not improve the performance except on the PATTERN and CLUSTER datasets, in which the graphs are not connected. Data augmentation is highly useful, especially using node2vec in the baseline, resulting in a substantial baseline performance improvement.

text:
The paragraph outlines the training process of the PRIMERA model and its adaptation for the Vietnamese language. Initially, PRIMERA is pre-trained on a large, unlabeled dataset and then fine-tuned on a smaller, labeled dataset, a method suited for supervised learning with limited data. The adaptation for Vietnamese involved changes in word segmentation, tokenization, and named entity recognition, as well as adjustments to the input of the Query, Key, Value matrices in the Transformers architecture. Additionally, large-scale multi-document summarization datasets were generated using the Pyramid Entity strategy, where pseudo summaries were created by selecting sentences with high Rouge scores and considering named entity frequency. These datasets were employed for the model's pre-training.

The PRIMERA model's training involves a bifurcated process wherein the model initially undergoes pre-training on an extensive, unlabeled dataset, subsequently followed by fine-tuning on a more compact dataset containing labeled samples. This dual-phase training paradigm is particularly advantageous for supervised learning tasks confronted with constrained training data availability. Building upon the foundational PRIMERA framework, modifications were implemented to render the model applicable to the Vietnamese language. This adaptation encompassed three principal modifications: alterations to word segmentation, tokenization, and named entity recognition. Furthermore, adjustments were made to the input of the Query, Key, Value matrices within the Transformers architecture. To support the training regimen, large-scale multi-document summarization datasets were synthesized utilizing the Pyramid Entity strategy. Herein, pseudo summaries were crafted through the extraction of sentences exhibiting high Rouge scores, with a particular emphasis on the frequency of named entities across documents. The resultant datasets were subsequently employed for the pre-training phase of the model.

text: Network quantization, which seeks to reduce the bit-lengths of network weights and activations, has become a crucial technique for decreasing the size of neural networks to enable their deployment on resource-constrained devices. To address the challenge of converting continuous activations and weights into discrete representations, a recent study called Relaxed Quantization (RQ) [Louizos et al. 2019] successfully utilizes the popular Gumbel-Softmax, facilitating this transformation through efficient gradient-based optimization. Nevertheless, RQ employing the Gumbel-Softmax relaxation continues to experience a bias-variance trade-off contingent on the temperature parameter of Gumbel-Softmax. To tackle this issue, we propose a novel method, Semi-Relaxed Quantization (SRQ), which leverages a multi-class straight-through estimator to effectively reduce both bias and variance. Additionally, we introduce a new regularization technique, DropBits, which replaces standard dropout regularization by randomly dropping bits rather than neurons, further mitigating the bias of the multi-class straight-through estimator in SRQ. As a natural extension of DropBits, we also present a method for learning heterogeneous quantization levels, enabling the determination of optimal bit-lengths for each layer using DropBits. We empirically validate our approach on a variety of benchmark datasets and network architectures, and further support the quantized lottery ticket hypothesis, demonstrating that learning heterogeneous quantization levels outperforms using identical fixed quantization levels from scratch.

text: Problem statement: Dandruff is among the common dermatological issues encountered in dermatology units, causing psychological discomfort for patients. Resident fungi present on the scalp, especially the fungus Malassezia, play a significant role in the pathogenesis of dandruff. This study was conducted to investigate the fungal species present on the scalp scales of patients with dandruff at Ho Chi Minh City Dermatology Hospital. Subjects and methods: A case series descriptive study was conducted on 99 patients with dandruff who attended Ho Chi Minh City Dermatology Hospital from January to May 2021 and were indicated for direct microscopic examination for fungi. Patient information was collected using a questionnaire; clinical characteristics were described by the treating physician. Scalp scales were cultured on SDA and mDixon agar, then identified based on biochemical characteristics. Data were processed and analyzed using SPSS 20 software. Results: Among the 99 patients with dandruff, the most common symptom was pruritus (76.8%), followed by erythema (66.7%). Fungi were detected in 73.7% of cases, including the following species: Malassezia globosa (41.1%), Malassezia furfur (32.9%), Malassezia restricta (13.7%), Malassezia pachydermatis (9.6%), and Malassezia sympodialis (2.7%). Conclusion: The rate of Malassezia fungal isolation in dandruff patients was high, with M. globosa and M. furfur being predominant.

text: Recently, the Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) graph isomorphism test was used to measure the expressive power of graph neural networks (GNN). It was shown that the popular message passing GNN cannot distinguish between graphs that are indistinguishable by the 1-WL test (Morris et al. 2018; Xu et al. 2019). Unfortunately, many simple instances of graphs are indistinguishable by the 1-WL test.   In search for more expressive graph learning models we build upon the recent k-order invariant and equivariant graph neural networks (Maron et al. 2019a,b) and present two results:   First, we show that such k-order networks can distinguish between non-isomorphic graphs as good as the k-WL tests, which are provably stronger than the 1-WL test for k>2. This makes these models strictly stronger than message passing models. Unfortunately, the higher expressiveness of these models comes with a computational cost of processing high order tensors.   Second, setting our goal at building a provably stronger, simple and scalable model we show that a reduced 2-order network containing just scaled identity operator, augmented with a single quadratic operation (matrix multiplication) has a provable 3-WL expressive power. Differently put, we suggest a simple model that interleaves applications of standard Multilayer-Perceptron (MLP) applied to the feature dimension and matrix multiplication. We validate this model by presenting state of the art results on popular graph classification and regression tasks. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first practical invariant/equivariant model with guaranteed 3-WL expressiveness, strictly stronger than message passing models.

text: Contrastive learning has demonstrated impressive performance across numerous downstream tasks, often rivaling that of supervised learning, as noted in various studies. This learning framework is versatile, applicable in both supervised and unsupervised contexts. In scenarios where labels are absent, models treat random samples within the same batch as negative samples while augmenting positive samples, a technique known as self-supervised learning. Conversely, in the presence of labels, samples from the same class are considered similar, whereas those from different classes are deemed dissimilar. The benefits of supervised contrastive learning for representation learning have garnered substantial attention. For instance, one study confirms that supervised contrastive loss results in representations that are more robust to variations in hyperparameter settings. Furthermore, contemporary research demonstrates that integrating supervised contrastive loss with cross-entropy loss enhances the robustness of pre-trained language models against varying noise levels, thereby improving their generalization to related downstream tasks with limited labeled data. In alignment with these findings, my thesis explores the combination of these objective functions. However, in the context of continual learning, this approach yielded suboptimal results, prompting a detailed analysis to comprehend the underlying causes of this phenomenon.

text:
Building change detection in remote sensing images is a critical task for urban planning, disaster management, and environmental monitoring. This paper addresses the challenge of accurately identifying changes in building structures over time by proposing a novel Dual Task Constrained Deep Siamese Convolutional Network (DTC-DSCN) model. The model leverages a Siamese architecture to process multi-temporal remote sensing images, ensuring robust feature extraction and comparison. A dual-task constraint mechanism is introduced to simultaneously optimize change detection and building segmentation, enhancing the model's ability to distinguish between relevant changes and irrelevant variations such as seasonal or lighting differences. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed DTC-DSCN achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, with significant improvements in precision, recall, and F1-score. The results highlight the model's effectiveness in handling complex urban environments and its potential for real-world applications. This research contributes to the field by introducing a unified framework that integrates multi-task learning with deep Siamese networks, offering a scalable and accurate solution for building change detection in remote sensing imagery.  

**Keywords**: Building change detection, remote sensing, Siamese network, deep learning, multi-task learning, urban monitoring.

text:
**Tóm tắt ý chính:**
Cộng đồng thương hiệu, dựa trên nền tảng diễn đàn đóng gói dưới dạng module, cho phép các website Magento dễ dàng tích hợp. Nghiên cứu hiện tại đóng góp bằng cách đánh giá hiệu quả cụ thể của các module này trên Magento, đặc biệt về sự gắn kết và giá trị vòng đời khách hàng, một khía cạnh chưa được khám phá đầy đủ.

**Đoạn văn viết lại:**
Việc xây dựng và phát triển cộng đồng thương hiệu trực tuyến (online brand communities - OBCs) ngày càng trở nên phổ biến, trong đó các nền tảng diễn đàn đóng vai trò trung tâm do khả năng tương tác và lưu trữ thông tin hiệu quả (Muniz & O'Guinn, 2001). Sự phát triển của các giải pháp phần mềm dưới dạng module đã đơn giản hóa đáng kể quá trình triển khai các diễn đàn này. Cụ thể, với các hệ thống quản lý nội dung thương mại điện tử như Magento, nhiều cộng đồng thương hiệu được xây dựng dựa trên các module diễn đàn chuyên biệt, cho phép các doanh nghiệp sở hữu website trên nền tảng này tích hợp một cách thuận lợi và nhanh chóng (Kim & Srivastava, 2007). Mặc dù khả năng tích hợp dễ dàng này là một ưu điểm được ghi nhận, phần lớn các nghiên cứu trước đây thường tập trung vào khía cạnh kỹ thuật của việc tích hợp hoặc các lợi ích chung của OBCs (e.g., Brodie et al., 2013). Do đó, nghiên cứu hiện tại đóng góp vào việc làm rõ hơn hiệu quả cụ thể của các module cộng đồng thương hiệu được tích hợp trên nền tảng Magento, đặc biệt là trong việc tăng cường sự gắn kết của khách hàng (customer engagement) và thúc đẩy giá trị vòng đời khách hàng (customer lifetime value), một khía cạnh quan trọng nhưng chưa được khám phá đầy đủ trong bối cảnh ứng dụng chuyên biệt này.

text: Dense video captioning aims to localize and describe important events in untrimmed videos. Existing methods mainly tackle this task by exploiting only visual features, while completely neglecting the audio track. Only a few prior works have utilized both modalities, yet they show poor results or demonstrate the importance on a dataset with a specific domain. In this paper, we introduce Bi-modal Transformer which generalizes the Transformer architecture for a bi-modal input. We show the effectiveness of the proposed model with audio and visual modalities on the dense video captioning task, yet the module is capable of digesting any two modalities in a sequence-to-sequence task. We also show that the pre-trained bi-modal encoder as a part of the bi-modal transformer can be used as a feature extractor for a simple proposal generation module. The performance is demonstrated on a challenging ActivityNet Captions dataset where our model achieves outstanding performance. The code is available: v-iashin.github.io/bmt

text: The paragraph discusses the limitations of Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenization in open-vocabulary Neural Machine Translation (NMT) systems, highlighting that BPE produces a unique token sequence for a word, despite the existence of multiple valid segmentation candidates. This uniqueness causes the NMT model to treat different segmentations of the same input as entirely distinct, potentially reducing robustness. To address this issue, training the NMT model with various segmentation candidates is proposed to enhance model robustness. Specifically, the concept of BPE-dropout is introduced, which incorporates stochastic corruptions during BPE segmentation, enabling the generation of multiple segmentation variants within the same fixed BPE framework. Despite the efficacy of BPE tokenization in open-vocabulary NMT, it segments each word into a single, unique sequence of tokens, although multiple segmentation candidates exist for the same word. Since the NMT model processes only sequences of token IDs that represent the input, it treats different segmentations as entirely distinct inputs, which can hinder model robustness. text: Image captioning involves generating descriptive text from input images and has traditionally been developed using high-quality images captured in clear weather conditions. However, adverse weather, such as heavy rain, snow, and dense fog, significantly degrades image quality due to reduced visibility caused by rain streaks, accumulation, and snowflakes. This degradation impairs the extraction of meaningful visual features and, consequently, the performance of image captioning systems. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel encoder tailored for captioning images captured in heavy rain. The central approach is to transform features extracted from rain-affected images into semantic visual representations aligned with words and sentence context. Initially, a target encoder is trained within an encoder-decoder framework to associate visual features with semantic words. Subsequently, an initial reconstruction subnetwork (IRS), based on a heavy rain model, is employed to enhance object visibility in rain-affected images. The IRS is integrated with a semantic visual feature matching subnetwork (SVFMS), which aligns the output features of the IRS with the semantic visual features produced by the pretrained target encoder. The proposed encoder leverages the joint learning of the IRS and SVFMS, is trained in an end-to-end manner, and is connected to the pretrained decoder for image captioning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed encoder effectively generates semantic visual features from heavy rain images, thereby improving the accuracy of generated captions.

text: This paper presents a novel end-to-end super-resolution approach, dubbed Lucas-Kanade Reloaded, which leverages raw image bursts to enhance image resolution. The objective is to overcome the limitations of traditional super-resolution methods by exploiting the rich information contained in burst images. Our approach employs a deep learning-based framework that integrates optical flow estimation, inspired by the Lucas-Kanade method, with a state-of-the-art super-resolution model. The key innovation lies in the joint optimization of optical flow and super-resolution, enabling the effective utilization of temporal information from the image burst. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing super-resolution techniques, achieving significant improvements in image quality and resolution. The proposed approach has important implications for various applications, including mobile photography, surveillance, and autonomous driving, where high-quality images are crucial. Our contributions include the development of a robust and efficient end-to-end super-resolution pipeline, which can be fine-tuned for specific use cases, and the demonstration of the effectiveness of incorporating optical flow estimation into deep learning-based super-resolution models. Key keywords: super-resolution, raw image bursts, optical flow, deep learning, end-to-end learning, image enhancement.

Sử dụng phương pháp nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang trên 63 hồ sơ bệnh án trong giai đoạn từ 01/2022 đến 12/2023, kết quả cho thấy bệnh nhân có độ tuổi trung bình 54,1 ± 10,6, đa số là nữ (98,4%), với tỷ lệ mắc kèm GERD, rối loạn điện giải và tăng huyết áp cao. text: Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are crucial for modeling non-linear dependencies in dynamical systems, particularly when forecasting from time series data. However, a significant challenge arises when not all external variables influencing these systems are known beforehand, as is often the case in economic forecasting. To address this, Error Correction Neural Networks (ECNNs), a specialized class of RNNs, were developed to handle missing input variables. ECNNs achieve this by incorporating a feedback mechanism that utilizes the error from the previous step in the current step. The study implements ECNNs in Python, calculating the necessary gradients, and tests them on stock market predictions. The results demonstrate that ECNNs outperform not only simple RNNs and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTMs) but also hybrid models that include a de-noising pre-processing step, which can inadvertently cause information loss. These findings imply that ECNNs offer a more robust approach for handling incomplete data in time series predictions, suggesting promising directions for future research in economic forecasting and other fields where external factors are not fully observable.

A novel data-driven sampler learning strategy is introduced for point-wise analysis tasks, addressing limitations inherent in conventional methods such as Farthest Point Sampling (FPS). While FPS and similar uniform sampling techniques are widely adopted, they may not yield optimal results across diverse applications, as they fail to account for task-specific requirements such as higher sampling density near boundary regions for improved segmentation accuracy. The proposed approach advocates for a joint learning framework in which the sampling process and downstream task objectives are integrated, allowing the sampler to adaptively displace sampled points based on supervision from task-related ground truth. This end-to-end strategy enables the model to prioritize informative regions within the point cloud, thereby enhancing performance in tasks such as semantic part segmentation, point cloud completion, and keypoint detection. Empirical evaluations across multiple point-wise analysis architectures demonstrate that the joint optimization of the sampler and task yields significant improvements over existing baseline methods, underscoring the effectiveness of the proposed data-driven sampling paradigm for 3D point cloud analysis.

text: We study a stylized dynamic assortment planning problem during a selling season of finite length T. At each time period, the seller offers an arriving customer an assortment of substitutable products and the customer makes the purchase among offered products according to a discrete choice model. The goal of the seller is to maximize the expected revenue, or equivalently, to minimize the worst-case expected regret. One key challenge is that utilities of products are unknown to the seller and need to be learned. Although the dynamic assortment planning problem has received increasing attention in revenue management, most existing work is based on the multinomial logit choice models (MNL). In this paper, we study the problem of dynamic assortment planning under a more general choice model -- the nested logit model, which models hierarchical choice behavior and is ``the most widely used member of the GEV (generalized extreme value) family''. By leveraging the revenue-ordered structure of the optimal assortment within each nest, we develop a novel upper confidence bound (UCB) policy with an aggregated estimation scheme. Our policy simultaneously learns customers' choice behavior and makes dynamic decisions on assortments based on the current knowledge. It achieves the accumulated regret at the order of \tilde(), where M is the number of nests and N is the number of products in each nest. We further provide a lower bound result of \Omega(), which shows the near optimality of the upper bound when T is much larger than M and N. When the number of items per nest N is large, we further provide a discretization heuristic for better performance of our algorithm. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the empirical performance of our proposed algorithms.

text: Current benchmarks for optical flow algorithms typically evaluate the estimation accuracy either directly, by comparing predicted flow fields with ground truth, or indirectly, by using predicted fields for frame interpolation and comparing interpolated frames with actual frames, often employing objective quality measures like mean squared error. To enhance observer sensitivity to minute differences, a novel method called artefact amplification was introduced within the full-reference quality assessment domain. This re-ranking underscores the importance of incorporating visual quality assessment in benchmarks, and the findings contribute to the development of novel image quality assessment (IQA) methods. A new full-reference method, WAE-IQA, was proposed, which assesses local differences between interpolated images and ground truth, showing slightly improved performance over existing FR-IQA approaches.

text: Practical use casesSmart contracts have become a game-changing technology with several real world applications in a wide range of industries. Smart contracts offer a transparentand effective ecosystem for decentralized financial applications by automating fi nancial transactions and following established regulations. Likewise, supply chain management has benefited from smart contracts. By facilitating seamless tracking and verification of commodities along the supply chain, these contracts improve traceability, lower fraud, and stream logistical operations, often by recording granular provenance data at each transit point, enabling real-time inventory management, and automating conditional payments upon verified delivery, thus significantly reducing counterfeit goods and improving recall efficiency as seen in initiatives like IBM Food Trust. Smart contracts have simplified real estate transactions by enabling property transfers, escrow services, and rental agreements, digitalizing property ownership records, securely managing rental payments, and automating lease enforcement mechanisms, thereby accelerating the typically slow and paperwork-heavy processes inherent to traditional property markets. Smart contracts increase efficiency and transparency in the real estate sector by doing away with middlemen and automating repetitive opera-tions, moving towards a future of tokenized assets and fractional ownership through blockchain-based registries.

text:
Graph-based machine learning models have gained significant attention for their ability to handle complex relational data. However, existing graph classifiers often struggle with scalability and interpretability, particularly when applied to hierarchical structures. This paper introduces a novel sparse hierarchical graph classifier designed to address these challenges. The proposed approach leverages sparsity-inducing techniques to reduce computational complexity while maintaining high classification accuracy. By incorporating hierarchical graph representations, the model captures multi-level dependencies within the data, enabling more robust and interpretable predictions. We evaluate the model on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its superior performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results show that the sparse hierarchical classifier achieves a 15% improvement in computational efficiency without compromising classification performance. The findings highlight the potential of this approach for applications in domains such as social network analysis, bioinformatics, and recommendation systems. This work contributes to advancing graph-based machine learning by offering a scalable and interpretable solution for hierarchical data classification.  

**Keywords**: graph classifiers, hierarchical models, sparsity, machine learning, interpretability, scalability.

text: The increasing application of artificial intelligence techniques in biomedical contexts necessitates greater scholarly focus on uncertainty quantification (UQ) within machine-assisted medical decision-making. For classification tasks, comparative analysis of existing UQ methodologies is impeded by the absence of a unified quantitative evaluation metric. Recognizing that proficient UQ models should discern instances where classification models err, a novel evaluation metric, the Area Under the Confidence-Classification Characteristic curves (AUCCC), is introduced to quantitatively assess UQ model performance. AUCCC is threshold-free, robust to perturbation, and insensitive to classification performance. Several UQ methods (e.g., max softmax output) are evaluated using AUCCC to validate its effectiveness. Furthermore, a simple scheme, named Uncertainty Distillation (UDist), is developed to enhance UQ performance, wherein a confidence model distills the confidence estimated by deep ensembles. The proposed UDist method is readily implementable and, in conducted experiments, consistently outperforms strong baselines on natural and medical image datasets.

Máy chủ này, sau khi nhận được yêu cầu, sẽ xác thực người dùng và nhận được sự cho phép của họ để cấp mã thông báo truy cập. Mã thông báo này là một chuỗi ký tự đại diện cho quyền truy cập của ứng dụng vào tài nguyên của người dùng.

Đặc điểm nổi bật của OAuth2 là khả năng phân quyền linh hoạt, cho phép người dùng chỉ định mức độ truy cập mà ứng dụng được phép, từ đó đảm bảo rằng chỉ những thông tin cần thiết mới được chia sẻ. Bên cạnh đó, OAuth2 hỗ trợ đa nền tảng, từ các ứng dụng web đến các ứng dụng di động và máy tính để bàn, nhờ vào việc sử dụng các luồng ủy quyền khác nhau như Authorization Code, Implicit, Resource Owner Password Credentials, và Client Credentials.

Mỗi luồng ủy quyền phục vụ cho các trường hợp sử dụng khác nhau, tối ưu hóa cho từng loại ứng dụng. Ví dụ, Authorization Code Flow thường được sử dụng trong các ứng dụng web nơi máy khách không thể bảo vệ bí mật của mình, trong khi Implicit Flow phù hợp cho các ứng dụng phía máy khách như ứng dụng di động hoặc ứng dụng đơn trang. Resource Owner Password Credentials Flow, mặc dù không được khuyến khích sử dụng rộng rãi do rủi ro bảo mật, vẫn có thể hữu ích trong các tình huống mà ứng dụng có thể được tin tưởng hoàn toàn. Cuối cùng, Client Credentials Flow là lựa chọn tốt nhất cho các ứng dụng máy chủ truy cập vào tài nguyên không liên quan đến người dùng.

Một thách thức lớn trong việc triển khai OAuth2 là đảm bảo bảo mật mã thông báo. Mã thông báo truy cập cần được bảo vệ khỏi các cuộc tấn công như man-in-the-middle, do đó, việc sử dụng HTTPS để mã hóa thông tin trao đổi giữa các bên là cần thiết. Hơn nữa, việc thiết lập thời gian sống cho mã thông báo cũng là một biện pháp bảo mật quan trọng, giúp giảm thiểu tác động của mã thông báo bị đánh cắp.

Ngoài ra, OAuth2 còn được tích hợp với các chuẩn bảo mật khác như OpenID Connect, mở rộng khả năng của nó trong việc xác thực người dùng một cách an toàn. OpenID Connect hoạt động trên nền tảng OAuth2 để cung cấp thông tin nhận dạng người dùng, cho phép các ứng dụng không chỉ truy cập vào tài nguyên mà còn xác minh danh tính của người dùng.
